title: Exodus Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Exodus chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Exodus Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Exodus Chapter 21.

questions.question: How many years shall a Hebrew servant serve before going out free?
options: Six years
Seven years
Five years
Ten years
questions.correctAnswer: Six years
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:2 states that a Hebrew servant shall serve six years and go out free in the seventh year.

questions.question: If a Hebrew servant came in married, who goes out with him when he is freed?
options: Only he goes out
His wife goes out with him
His children go out with him
His wife and children go out with him
questions.correctAnswer: His wife goes out with him
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:3 explains that if the servant was married when he came in, then his wife shall go out with him.

questions.question: If a master gives a servant a wife and she bears him children, who do the wife and children belong to after the servant goes out?
options: They go out with the servant
They belong to the servant
They belong to the master
They belong to the servant's family
questions.correctAnswer: They belong to the master
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:4 states that if the servant's master gave him a wife and she bore children, the wife and children shall be the master's.

questions.question: What must a servant say if he chooses to remain with his master and not go out free?
options: "I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free"
"I want to stay and serve more years"
"I refuse to leave because I owe debts"
"I wish to be adopted by my master"
questions.correctAnswer: "I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free"
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:5 records the servant plainly saying, "I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free."

questions.question: What is done to a servant who chooses to stay with his master forever?
options: He is given a new contract
His ear is bored through with an aul at the doorpost
He is given land
He is given a new wife
questions.correctAnswer: His ear is bored through with an aul at the doorpost
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:6 describes that the master shall bore his ear through with an aul at the doorpost, signifying he shall serve forever.

questions.question: If a man sells his daughter to be a maidservant, how does her going out differ from male servants?
options: She goes out free after six years like male servants
She does not go out as the menservants do
She must serve only three years
She is freed immediately
questions.correctAnswer: She does not go out as the menservants do
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:7 states that a maidservant sold as a daughter shall not go out as the menservants do.

questions.question: What must a master do if his maidservant does not please him, but he has betrothed her to himself?
options: Sell her to a stranger
Redeem her and not sell her to a strange nation
Keep her regardless
Let her go free immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Redeem her and not sell her to a strange nation
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:8 commands that if she does not please her master, he must let her be redeemed and cannot sell her to a strange nation.

questions.question: If a man takes another wife, what must he not diminish for the first wife?
options: Her freedom
Her food, raiment, and duty of marriage
Her property rights
Her children
questions.correctAnswer: Her food, raiment, and duty of marriage
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:10 states that if a man takes another wife, he must not diminish the first wife's food, raiment, or duty of marriage.

questions.question: True or False: A man who kills another by striking him shall be put to death.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:12 clearly states that he who smiteth a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death.

questions.question: True or False: If a man kills another without lying in wait, God will provide a place for the killer to flee.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:13 says if a man does not lie in wait but God delivers him into the other's hand, a place of refuge shall be appointed.

questions.question: True or False: A man who strikes his father or mother shall be punished but not put to death.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:15 states that he who smiteth his father or mother shall surely be put to death.

questions.question: True or False: A man who steals another man and sells him shall be put to death.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:16 commands that he who stealeth a man and sell him shall surely be put to death.

questions.question: Which of the following instructions comes first in Exodus 21?
options: Punishment for killing a man
The length of service for a Hebrew servant
Rules about selling a daughter as a maidservant
Instructions about an ox goring a man
questions.correctAnswer: The length of service for a Hebrew servant
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:2 comes before the other instructions listed, addressing the Hebrew servant's service length.

questions.question: If a servant loves his master, wife, and children and chooses to stay, what symbolic act is performed?
options: He is given a special ring
His ear is bored through with an aul
He signs a contract
He is given land
questions.correctAnswer: His ear is bored through with an aul
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:6 states the master shall bore his ear through with an aul to signify he will serve forever.

questions.question: If a man sells his daughter as a maidservant and she is betrothed to his son, how is she treated?
options: As a servant like the menservants
As a daughter
As a stranger
As a wife only
questions.correctAnswer: As a daughter
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:9 says if the maidservant is betrothed to the master's son, she shall be dealt with as a daughter.

medium.title: Exodus Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Exodus Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Exodus 21:13, what provision is made for a man who kills another without premeditation, when God delivers the victim into his hand?
options: He shall be put to death immediately
He shall flee to a designated place of refuge
He shall pay a ransom to the victim's family
He shall be forgiven and released
questions.correctAnswer: He shall flee to a designated place of refuge
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:13 states that if a man kills without lying in wait, God delivering the victim into his hand, a place shall be appointed where he can flee. This shows provision for accidental manslaughter, unlike premeditated murder (Exodus 21:14), which requires death.

questions.question: What is the consequence described in Exodus 21:14 for a man who kills his neighbor with guile, even if he seeks refuge at the altar?
options: He shall be forgiven if he offers a sacrifice
He shall be taken from the altar and put to death
He shall pay a fine to the victim's family
He shall be exiled from the community
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be taken from the altar and put to death
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:14 makes clear that a person who kills with guile has no protection even at the altar and must be taken away to die. This contrasts with accidental killing in verse 13 and emphasizes justice for intentional murder.

questions.question: What punishment does Exodus 21:15 prescribe for one who strikes his father or mother?
options: He shall be fined
He shall be put to death
He shall be publicly shamed
He shall be imprisoned
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be put to death
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:15 commands that anyone who smites his father or mother shall be surely put to death, underscoring the importance of honoring parents as a biblical virtue (also seen in Exodus 21:17 about cursing parents).

questions.question: According to Exodus 21:16, what is the penalty for stealing a person and selling them?
options: A heavy fine
Imprisonment until restitution is made
Death
Exile from the community
questions.correctAnswer: Death
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:16 states that stealing a man and selling him, or having him found in one's possession, results in death, highlighting the severity of this crime and the value placed on human life.

questions.question: What does Exodus 21:17 say about the one who curses his father or mother?
options: He shall be disciplined by the community
He shall be put to death
He shall be forgiven after repentance
He shall be fined
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be put to death
questions.explanation: The verse commands the death penalty for cursing parents, reinforcing the biblical value of honoring and respecting one's parents (also Exodus 21:15). This reflects the gravity of dishonoring family relationships.

questions.question: According to Exodus 21:18-19, if two men fight and one injures the other but he recovers and walks again, what is the consequence for the one who caused the injury?
options: He shall be put to death
He shall pay for lost time and ensure full healing
He shall be imprisoned for a time
He shall be forgiven without penalty
questions.correctAnswer: He shall pay for lost time and ensure full healing
questions.explanation: Verses 18 and 19 explain that if the injured man recovers and walks with a staff, the offender is not punished by death but must compensate for lost time and make sure the victim is fully healed, emphasizing responsibility and restitution.

questions.question: What does Exodus 21:20-21 teach about the treatment of servants who suffer injury or death from their masters?
options: Masters are never punished for injuring servants
Masters who kill servants must be punished, but if the servant survives a day or two, punishment is not required
Servants have no legal protection
Injuries to servants are always punishable by death
questions.correctAnswer: Masters who kill servants must be punished, but if the servant survives a day or two, punishment is not required
questions.explanation: Verse 20 mandates punishment if a servant dies under a master's hand, but verse 21 exempts punishment if the servant lives a day or two, reflecting the value of property but also a limit on the master's power.

questions.question: If a pregnant woman is injured during a fight and her child is lost but no further harm follows, what does Exodus 21:22 prescribe?
options: The offender must be put to death
The offender shall be punished and pay as the woman's husband and judges decide
No punishment is required
The woman must forgive the offender
questions.correctAnswer: The offender shall be punished and pay as the woman's husband and judges decide
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:22 prescribes punishment and compensation as determined by the husband and judges if the child is lost but no further harm occurs, emphasizing justice and restitution without capital punishment.

questions.question: How does Exodus 21:23-24 define the principle of justice for cases where injury causes further harm?
options: Forgiveness and reconciliation
Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot
Monetary compensation only
Exile of the offender
questions.correctAnswer: Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot
questions.explanation: These verses establish the lex talionis principle of proportional justice, requiring equivalent punishment to the harm caused, emphasizing fairness and deterrence in biblical law.

questions.question: What does Exodus 21:26-27 say must happen if a master injures the eye or tooth of his servant?
options: The servant must continue to serve without compensation
The master must let the servant go free because of the injury
The servant shall receive a monetary fine
The master must pay the servant's medical expenses
questions.correctAnswer: The master must let the servant go free because of the injury
questions.explanation: These verses require that if a master causes loss of an eye or tooth to a servant, the servant must be freed as compensation for the injury, showing concern for the servant's welfare and justice.

questions.question: According to Exodus 21:28-29, what is the difference in consequences for an ox that kills a person when the ox was known to be dangerous versus when it was not?
options: No difference in consequences
The ox is stoned in both cases, but the owner is put to death only if he knew of the danger and did not restrain it
The ox is sold to pay a fine in both cases
Only the ox is punished, regardless of the owner's knowledge
questions.correctAnswer: The ox is stoned in both cases, but the owner is put to death only if he knew of the danger and did not restrain it
questions.explanation: Verses 28-29 explain that all oxen that kill are stoned, but if the owner knew the ox's dangerous habits and failed to keep it restrained, the owner also faces death, emphasizing responsibility for prevention.

questions.question: What does Exodus 21:30-31 provide as an alternative to the death penalty for a negligent owner whose ox kills a person, when a ransom is laid upon him?
options: The owner must be imprisoned for life
The owner must pay the ransom money to redeem his life
The owner is immediately put to death without ransom
The owner must give another ox to the victim's family
questions.correctAnswer: The owner must pay the ransom money to redeem his life
questions.explanation: These verses allow for a ransom payment as a means to redeem the life of the owner when his ox kills someone, showing a provision for mercy and compensation in certain cases.

questions.question: How does Exodus 21:32 instruct regarding compensation when an ox kills a servant or maidservant?
options: The servant or maidservant's family must be compensated
The owner of the ox shall pay thirty shekels of silver to the master, and the ox shall be stoned
The ox is released and the owner pays nothing
The owner must replace the servant or maidservant
questions.correctAnswer: The owner of the ox shall pay thirty shekels of silver to the master, and the ox shall be stoned
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:32 prescribes a specific silver payment to the master of the servant or maidservant killed by the ox, alongside the ox being stoned, reflecting justice and restitution for loss of property.

questions.question: If a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox falls in and dies, what responsibility does the owner of the pit have according to Exodus 21:33-34?
options: No responsibility if the animal falls accidentally
He must compensate the owner of the ox, and the dead ox belongs to him
He must replace the ox with a new one
He must pay a fine to the community
questions.correctAnswer: He must compensate the owner of the ox, and the dead ox belongs to him
questions.explanation: These verses state the pit owner must make restitution for the lost animal, but the dead animal remains his, emphasizing responsibility for unsafe conditions and fair compensation.

questions.question: What does Exodus 21:35-36 say about the ownership and compensation if one's ox kills another ox, and it was known to be dangerous?
options: The owner of the dangerous ox pays ox for ox, and keeps the dead one
Both owners share the loss equally
The dangerous ox is sold and the money divided
The owner of the killed ox receives no compensation
questions.correctAnswer: The owner of the dangerous ox pays ox for ox, and keeps the dead one
questions.explanation: These verses require the owner of a known dangerous ox who fails to restrain it to pay another ox for the one killed, while the dead ox remains with the owner of the killed ox, emphasizing accountability.

hard.title: Exodus Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Exodus Chapter 21.

questions.question: According to Exodus 21:26, what must a master do if he smites out the eye of his servant?
options: Let the servant go free for his eye's sake
Pay a fine to the servant
Punish the servant
Replace the servant with another
questions.correctAnswer: Let the servant go free for his eye's sake
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:26 states that if a man smites out the eye of his servant, he shall let him go free for his eye's sake, meaning the servant is granted freedom as compensation for the injury.

questions.question: What is the penalty for killing a man by striking him, according to Exodus 21:12?
options: The offender shall be put to death
The offender must pay a ransom
The offender shall be imprisoned
The offender must serve as a servant
questions.correctAnswer: The offender shall be put to death
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:12 commands that he who smites a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death, indicating the law of capital punishment for murder.

questions.question: Which verse in Exodus 21 establishes the principle of 'eye for eye, tooth for tooth'?
options: Exodus 21:24
Exodus 21:22
Exodus 21:18
Exodus 21:27
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 21:24
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:24 explicitly states 'Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,' establishing the lex talionis principle of equitable retribution.

questions.question: If a man digs a pit and does not cover it, causing an ox or ass to fall in, what is the responsibility of the pit owner according to Exodus 21:34?
options: He must make restitution and pay money to the owner
He shall be put to death
He must give an animal as compensation
He is not responsible
questions.correctAnswer: He must make restitution and pay money to the owner
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:34 states that the owner of the pit shall make it good and give money to the owner of the animal, with the dead beast becoming the pit owner's property.

questions.question: According to Exodus 21:29, what happens if an ox known to be dangerous kills a man or woman and the owner did not restrain it?
options: The ox shall be stoned and the owner put to death
Only the ox shall be killed
The owner must pay a ransom
The owner is excused
questions.correctAnswer: The ox shall be stoned and the owner put to death
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:29 prescribes that if an ox known to push with its horn kills a person and the owner failed to keep it confined, both the ox and the owner shall be put to death, showing responsibility for negligence.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'servant' in Exodus 21:2 imply in the cultural context of ancient Israel?
options: A bondservant with limited term of service
A slave for life without rights
A hired laborer with wages
A free citizen working voluntarily
questions.correctAnswer: A bondservant with limited term of service
questions.explanation: In the Hebrew context of Exodus 21:2, 'servant' (עֶבֶד, eved) often refers to a bondservant who serves for six years and is freed in the seventh, reflecting social and economic conditions of ancient Israel.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the principle of 'eye for eye' found in Exodus 21:24 by calling believers to a higher standard of forgiveness?
options: Matthew 5:38-39
Romans 13:4
James 2:13
Hebrews 10:30
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 5:38-39
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:38-39 references the 'eye for eye' law from Exodus 21:24 but instructs believers to not resist evil and turn the other cheek, revealing Jesus' fulfillment and reinterpretation of the law.

questions.question: What does Exodus 21:22-23 say regarding injury to a pregnant woman during a fight and its consequences?
options: If no further harm follows, a penalty is paid; if harm follows, life for life
The offender is always put to death
The injured woman must forgive the offender
There is no penalty if the child is lost
questions.correctAnswer: If no further harm follows, a penalty is paid; if harm follows, life for life
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:22-23 differentiates between causing a miscarriage without further harm, which incurs a fine, and if further harm follows, the law demands life for life, showing graded justice.

questions.question: In the literary structure of Exodus 21, what literary device is exemplified by the repeated phrase 'he shall be surely put to death' in verses like 12, 15, and 17?
options: Repetition for emphasis
Chiasmus
Parallelism
Metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Repetition for emphasis
questions.explanation: The phrase 'he shall be surely put to death' is repeated in Exodus 21:12, 15, and 17 to emphasize the seriousness of offenses such as murder and cursing parents, underscoring the death penalty.

questions.question: According to Exodus 21:36, what is the required compensation if an ox known for pushing kills another ox and the owner did not restrain it?
options: The owner shall pay ox for ox
The owner is excused
Only the dead ox is compensated
The owner must offer a sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: The owner shall pay ox for ox
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:36 states that if an ox known for pushing kills another ox and the owner failed to keep it in, he must pay 'ox for ox,' meaning full restitution for the loss.

questions.question: What is the significance of the aul (awl) used in Exodus 21:6 when a servant chooses to remain with his master?
options: It symbolizes permanent servitude by piercing the ear
It is a tool for punishment
It signifies transfer of ownership
It is used for branding the servant
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes permanent servitude by piercing the ear
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:6 describes the master piercing the servant’s ear with an aul (awl) at the doorpost to symbolize the servant's voluntary lifelong service, marking a permanent covenant.

questions.question: True or False: Exodus 21:21 states that if a servant dies after being beaten but after a day or two, the master shall not be punished.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:21 indicates that if a servant survives a beating for a day or two and then dies, the master is not punished because the servant is considered his money, reflecting the harsh realities of servitude.

questions.question: In Exodus 21:28-29, how is the principle of owner liability for an animal's actions developed?
options: Liability depends on the owner's knowledge and control of the animal
Owners are always liable regardless of circumstances
Owners are never liable for animals
Liability is transferred to the animal itself
questions.correctAnswer: Liability depends on the owner's knowledge and control of the animal
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:28-29 distinguishes between an ox that kills without prior warning and one known to be dangerous, making the owner liable only if he failed to restrain the animal after being warned.

questions.question: Which verse in Exodus 21 emphasizes the protection of family when a servant is freed, stating that if he came in married, his wife shall go out with him?
options: Exodus 21:3
Exodus 21:4
Exodus 21:5
Exodus 21:7
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 21:3
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:3 specifies that if an Hebrew servant came in married, his wife shall go out with him when he is freed, protecting the family unit upon release.

questions.question: True or False: Exodus 21:16 states that stealing a man and selling him is punishable by death.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:16 declares that he who steals a man and sells him, or is found in possession of him, shall surely be put to death, underscoring the gravity of kidnapping and slave trading.

theological.title: Exodus Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Exodus Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Exodus 21:2, what is the maximum duration an Hebrew servant should serve before going free?
options: Six years
Seven years
Ten years
Five years
questions.correctAnswer: Six years
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:2 states that an Hebrew servant shall serve six years and in the seventh year shall go out free.

questions.question: What theological principle is demonstrated by the law in Exodus 21:6 regarding a servant who loves his master and chooses to stay?
options: Perpetual voluntary servitude as a symbol of covenant faithfulness
Mandatory release regardless of feelings
Freedom from all earthly masters
The servant must become a priest
questions.correctAnswer: Perpetual voluntary servitude as a symbol of covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:5-6 show that if a servant declares love for his master and family, he may choose to serve forever, signifying voluntary commitment and covenant loyalty.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by the command in Exodus 21:12 that 'He that smiteth a man, so that he die, shall be surely put to death'?
options: The sanctity of human life and the justice of capital punishment
The forgiveness of all offenses
Absolute pacifism
Priestly mediation for offenders
questions.correctAnswer: The sanctity of human life and the justice of capital punishment
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:12 illustrates God's regard for human life and establishes capital punishment for intentional killing, reflecting divine justice.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed in Exodus 21:22-23 where the law prescribes punishment for causing miscarriage and harm to a woman with child?
options: God's justice and mercy
God's wrath alone
God's indifference
God's sovereignty over nature
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice and mercy
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:22-23 reveals God's justice in punishing harm and His mercy in proportioning the punishment according to the injury caused.

questions.question: How does Exodus 21:26-27 reflect the doctrine of restitution and human dignity?
options: Injuries to a servant's eye or tooth require the servant's freedom
Servants have no rights
Only monetary fines are required
Injuries are to be ignored
questions.correctAnswer: Injuries to a servant's eye or tooth require the servant's freedom
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:26-27 mandates that if a master harms a servant's eye or tooth, the servant must be freed, showing the value of human dignity and restitution.

questions.question: Considering Exodus 21:28-29, what does the different treatment of an ox that has previously gored reveal about personal responsibility?
options: Owners are accountable for known dangers their property poses
Animals are always punished instead of owners
There is no responsibility for accidental harm
Only monetary compensation is required
questions.correctAnswer: Owners are accountable for known dangers their property poses
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:29 assigns death penalty to the owner if they neglect to restrain a dangerous ox, showing responsibility for known hazards.

questions.question: What combined teaching about servitude and family responsibility is conveyed by Exodus 21:3-4 and Exodus 21:7-9?
options: Servants' family situations affect their freedom and treatment, recognizing family continuity and dignity
Servants have no family rights
All servants must leave family behind
Family is irrelevant in servitude laws
questions.correctAnswer: Servants' family situations affect their freedom and treatment, recognizing family continuity and dignity
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:3-4 and 7-9 distinguish between servants who come single or married and the rights of maidservants, emphasizing family status affects servitude outcomes.

questions.question: What does Exodus 21:10-11 teach about the master's obligations towards a wife given to a servant?
options: The master must maintain her food, raiment, and marital rights or she goes free
The wife has no rights
The servant must provide for her
The wife can be sold to others
questions.correctAnswer: The master must maintain her food, raiment, and marital rights or she goes free
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:10-11 require that the master's provision to the wife must not diminish; failure results in her freedom, reflecting justice and care in relationships.

questions.question: How does the law in Exodus 21:20-21 display a tension between property rights and human dignity?
options: It punishes a master if a servant dies under his hand but not if the servant recovers, showing a limited view of servant's value
It grants full equality to servants
It forbids any corporal punishment
It treats servants as mere objects
questions.correctAnswer: It punishes a master if a servant dies under his hand but not if the servant recovers, showing a limited view of servant's value
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:20-21 punishes death of a servant due to beating but not minor injury, reflecting the servant's status as property but still protected under the law.

questions.question: In the narrative of Exodus 21, how does the provision for cities of refuge in Exodus 21:13 connect to God's redemptive justice?
options: It offers protection for accidental killers, showing God's mercy within justice
It demands death for all killings
It removes any punishment for murder
It is unrelated to God's justice
questions.correctAnswer: It offers protection for accidental killers, showing God's mercy within justice
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:13 provides a refuge for those who kill unintentionally, reflecting God's balance of justice and mercy in the law.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by the principle 'eye for eye, tooth for tooth' in Exodus 21:24?
options: God's justice and fairness in punishment
God's unrestrained wrath
God's unconditional forgiveness
God's indifference
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice and fairness in punishment
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:24 outlines proportional justice, showing God's attribute of fair and measured retribution.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Exodus 21:15 and Exodus 21:17 offer about honoring parents and divine justice?
options: Cursing or striking parents is a capital offense, emphasizing the sanctity of parental authority
Parents have no special status
Only physical abuse is punished
Parents must forgive all offenses
questions.correctAnswer: Cursing or striking parents is a capital offense, emphasizing the sanctity of parental authority
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:15 and 17 prescribe death for striking or cursing parents, underscoring the sacred respect owed to parents and God's strict justice.

questions.question: How do Exodus 21:33-36 reveal God's concern for neighborly responsibility and property damage?
options: Owners must compensate for damages their property causes, showing accountability
No compensation is required
Property damage is irrelevant
God punishes animals directly
questions.correctAnswer: Owners must compensate for damages their property causes, showing accountability
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:33-36 require owners to make restitution for property-caused injury or death, reflecting responsibility and justice in human relationships.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Exodus 21:21 shows a disregard for servant's life by stating masters shall not be punished if the servant survives a beating. What does Exodus 21:20-21 actually teach about the value of servants?
options: It teaches limited protection of servants' lives but acknowledges their value as property
It condones abuse without consequence
It demands equal treatment of servants and free men
It allows unlimited beating
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches limited protection of servants' lives but acknowledges their value as property
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:20-21 shows servants as property yet with legal protection against death by beating, reflecting a complex valuation of human life in ancient law.

questions.question: What theological theme is emphasized by the servant's ear being bored with an aul in Exodus 21:6?
options: Permanent commitment and covenant loyalty
Punishment for rebellion
Release from all obligations
Symbolic cleansing
questions.correctAnswer: Permanent commitment and covenant loyalty
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:6 uses the symbolic piercing of the ear to indicate lifelong voluntary servitude, reflecting commitment and faithfulness.
